cudaLaunchMemSyncDomain.doc:
Memory Synchronization Domain.

A kernel can be launched in a specified memory synchronization domain that affects all memory operations issued by that kernel. A memory barrier issued in one domain will only order memory operations in that domain, thus eliminating latency increase from memory barriers ordering unrelated traffic.

By default, kernels are launched in domain 0. Kernel launched with [cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainRemote](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggaafb98f7ea7b0397ed6503780f3e672d5aac477b14c4ce022e029a4c2523eaeec2) will have a different domain ID. User may also alter the domain ID with [cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainMap](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaLaunchMemSyncDomainMap.html#structcudalaunchmemsyncdomainmap) for a specific stream / graph node / kernel launch. See [cudaLaunchAttributeMemSyncDomain](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggafc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056a4cf7f560204bcd328e64214e3c82a416), [cudaStreamSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1gabe4c1a2ce58f747d8fdffe6bc2ed3b32), [cudaLaunchKernelEx](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__cudart__highlevel_1ga7d9168c86a4293639c75ea437465ed53), [cudaGraphKernelNodeSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__cudart__graph_1gace65f436d34408075efbec0f468878ca).

Memory operations done in kernels launched in different domains are considered system-scope distanced. In other words, a GPU scoped memory synchronization is not sufficient for memory order to be observed by kernels in another memory synchronization domain even if they are on the same GPU.

cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainDefault.doc: Launch kernels in the default domain.

cudaLaunchMemSyncDomainRemote.doc: Launch kernels in the remote domain.

cudaLibraryOption.doc: Library options to be specified with [cudaLibraryLoadData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__LIBRARY.html#group__cudart__library_1ga4d75bf17458de4d4920cfb985b6f9cba) or [cudaLibraryLoadFromFile()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__LIBRARY.html#group__cudart__library_1ga69daf14fb4274286c8c1c7c1890c27cf).

cudaLibraryBinaryIsPreserved.doc:
Specifes that the argument `code` passed to [cudaLibraryLoadData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__LIBRARY.html#group__cudart__library_1ga4d75bf17458de4d4920cfb985b6f9cba) will be preserved.

Specifying this option will let the driver know that `code` can be accessed at any point until [cudaLibraryUnload()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__LIBRARY.html#group__cudart__library_1ga16568757be5aeb7f32a9c98f2976a28d). The default behavior is for the driver to allocate and maintain its own copy of `code`. Note that this is only a memory usage optimization hint and the driver can choose to ignore it if required. Specifying this option with [cudaLibraryLoadFromFile()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__LIBRARY.html#group__cudart__library_1ga69daf14fb4274286c8c1c7c1890c27cf) is invalid and will return [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c).

cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount.doc: GPU device runtime pending launch count.

cudaLimitMaxL2FetchGranularity.doc:
A value between 0 and 128 that indicates the maximum fetch granularity of L2 (in Bytes).

This is a hint.

cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize.doc: A size in bytes for L2 persisting lines cache size.

cudaMemAccessFlags.doc: Specifies the memory protection flags for mapping.

cudaMemAccessFlagsProtNone.doc: Default, make the address range not accessible.

cudaMemAccessFlagsProtRead.doc: Make the address range read accessible.

cudaMemAccessFlagsProtReadWrite.doc: Make the address range read-write accessible.

cudaMemAllocationHandleType.doc: Flags for specifying particular handle types.

cudaMemHandleTypeNone.doc:
Does not allow any export mechanism.

>.

cudaMemHandleTypePosixFileDescriptor.doc:
Allows a file descriptor to be used for exporting.

Permitted only on POSIX systems. (int).

cudaMemHandleTypeWin32.doc:
Allows a Win32 NT handle to be used for exporting.

(HANDLE).

cudaMemHandleTypeWin32Kmt.doc:
Allows a Win32 KMT handle to be used for exporting.

(D3DKMT_HANDLE).

cudaMemHandleTypeFabric.doc:
Allows a fabric handle to be used for exporting.

([cudaMemFabricHandle_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaMemFabricHandle__t.html#structcudamemfabrichandle__t)).

cudaMemAllocationTypePinned.doc:
This allocation type is ‘pinned’, i.e.

cannot migrate from its current location while the application is actively using it.

cudaMemAllocationTypeManaged.doc: This allocation type is managed memory.

cudaMemLocationTypeNone.doc:
Location is unspecified.

This is used when creating a managed memory pool to indicate no preferred location for the pool.

cudaMemLocationTypeDevice.doc: Location is a device location, thus id is a device ordinal.

cudaMemLocationTypeHost.doc: Location is host, id is ignored.

cudaMemLocationTypeHostNuma.doc: Location is a host NUMA node, thus id is a host NUMA node id.

cudaMemLocationTypeHostNumaCurrent.doc: Location is the host NUMA node closest to the current thread’s CPU, id is ignored.

cudaMemLocationTypeInvisible.doc: Location is not visible but device is accessible, id is always cudaInvalidDeviceId.

cudaMemLocationTypeDeviceLocalityDomain.doc: Location is a portion of device memory, specified by the locality domain ID.

cudaMemPoolReuseFollowEventDependencies.doc:
(value type = int) Allow cuMemAllocAsync to use memory asynchronously freed in another streams as long as a stream ordering dependency of the allocating stream on the free action exists.

CUDA events and null stream interactions can create the required stream ordered dependencies. (default enabled).

cudaMemPoolReuseAllowOpportunistic.doc:
(value type = int) Allow reuse of already completed frees when there is no dependency between the free and allocation.

(default enabled).

cudaMemPoolReuseAllowInternalDependencie.doc: (value type = int) Allow cuMemAllocAsync to insert new stream dependencies in order to establish the stream ordering required to reuse a piece of memory released by cuFreeAsync (default enabled).

cudaMemPoolAttrReleaseThreshold.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of reserved memory in bytes to hold onto before trying to release memory back to the OS.

When more than the release threshold bytes of memory are held by the memory pool, the allocator will try to release memory back to the OS on the next call to stream, event or context synchronize. (default 0).

cudaMemPoolAttrReservedMemCurrent.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of backing memory currently allocated for the mempool.

cudaMemPoolAttrReservedMemHigh.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of backing memory allocated for the mempool since the last time it was reset.

High watermark can only be reset to zero.

cudaMemPoolAttrUsedMemCurrent.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of memory from the pool that is currently in use by the application.

cudaMemPoolAttrUsedMemHigh.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of the amount of memory from the pool that was in use by the application since the last time it was reset.

High watermark can only be reset to zero.

cudaMemPoolAttrAllocationType.doc: (value type = cudaMemAllocationType) The allocation type of the mempool.

cudaMemPoolAttrExportHandleTypes.doc:
(value type = cudaMemAllocationHandleType) Available export handle types for the mempool.

For imported pools this value is always cudaMemHandleTypeNone as an imported pool cannot be re-exported.

cudaMemPoolAttrLocationId.doc:
(value type = int) The location id for the mempool.

If the location type for this pool is cudaMemLocationTypeInvisible then ID will be cudaInvalidDeviceId.

cudaMemPoolAttrLocationType.doc:
(value type = cudaMemLocationType) The location type for the mempool.

For imported memory pools where the device is not directly visible to the importing process or pools imported via fabric handles across nodes this will be cudaMemLocationTypeInvisible.

cudaMemPoolAttrMaxPoolSize.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) Maximum size of the pool in bytes, this value may be higher than what was initially passed to cudaMemPoolCreate due to alignment requirements.

A value of 0 indicates no maximum size. For cudaMemAllocationTypeManaged and IPC imported pools this value will be system dependent.

cudaMemPoolAttrHwDecompressEnabled.doc: (value type = int) Indicates whether the pool has hardware compresssion enabled.

cudaMemPoolAttrLocalityDomainId.doc:
(value type = int) The locality domain id for the mempool, if the mempool is localized to a locality domain.

A value of -1 indicates that the mempool is not localized to a locality domain.

cudaMemRangeAttributeReadMostly.doc: Whether the range will mostly be read and only occassionally be written to.

cudaMemRangeAttributePreferredLocation.doc: The preferred location of the range.

cudaMemRangeAttributeAccessedBy.doc: Memory range has [cudaMemAdviseSetAccessedBy](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggac314a8b14091f7e02a7ad15dcb36c857a50a22279bce0dc29956ad4f257084623) set for specified device.

cudaMemRangeAttributeLastPrefetchLocatio.doc: The last location to which the range was prefetched.

cudaMemRangeAttributePreferredLocationTy.doc: The preferred location type of the range.

cudaMemRangeAttributePreferredLocationId.doc: The preferred location id of the range.

cudaMemRangeAttributeLastPrefetchLocatio.doc: The last location type to which the range was prefetched.
The last location id to which the range was prefetched.

cudaMemcpy3DOperandType.doc: These flags allow applications to convey the operand type for individual copies specified in [cudaMemcpy3DBatchAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga9b3b66be1f930f77f717e54783573f9a).

cudaMemcpyOperandTypePointer.doc: Memcpy operand is a valid pointer.

cudaMemcpyFlags.doc:
Flags to specify for copies within a batch.

For more details see [cudaMemcpyBatchAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga6126baf5d881835091c59e48890d6854).

cudaMemcpyFlagPreferOverlapWithCompute.doc: Hint to the driver to try and overlap the copy with compute work on the SMs.

cudaMemcpyDefault.doc:
Direction of the transfer is inferred from the pointer values.

Requires unified virtual addressing.

cudaMemcpySrcAccessOrderStream.doc: Indicates that access to the source pointer must be in stream order.

cudaMemcpySrcAccessOrderDuringApiCall.doc:
Indicates that access to the source pointer can be out of stream order and all accesses must be complete before the API call returns.

This flag is suited for ephemeral sources (ex., stack variables) when it’s known that no prior operations in the stream can be accessing the memory and also that the lifetime of the memory is limited to the scope that the source variable was declared in. Specifying this flag allows the driver to optimize the copy and removes the need for the user to synchronize the stream after the API call.

cudaMemcpySrcAccessOrderAny.doc:
Indicates that access to the source pointer can be out of stream order and the accesses can happen even after the API call returns.

This flag is suited for host pointers allocated outside CUDA (ex., via malloc) when it’s known that no prior operations in the stream can be accessing the memory. Specifying this flag allows the driver to optimize the copy on certain platforms.

cudaMemAdviseSetReadMostly.doc: Data will mostly be read and only occassionally be written to.

cudaMemAdviseSetPreferredLocation.doc: Set the preferred location for the data as the specified device.

cudaMemAdviseUnsetPreferredLocation.doc: Clear the preferred location for the data.

cudaMemAdviseSetAccessedBy.doc: Data will be accessed by the specified device, so prevent page faults as much as possible.

cudaMemAdviseUnsetAccessedBy.doc: Let the Unified Memory subsystem decide on the page faulting policy for the specified device.

cudaResViewFormatNone.doc: No resource view format (use underlying resource format).

cudaSharedCarveout.doc:
Shared memory carveout configurations.

These may be passed to cudaFuncSetAttribute.

cudaSharedmemCarveoutDefault.doc: No preference for shared memory or L1 (default).

cudaSharedmemCarveoutMaxShared.doc: Prefer maximum available shared memory, minimum L1 cache.

cudaSharedmemCarveoutMaxL1.doc: Prefer maximum available L1 cache, minimum shared memory.

cudaSharedMemoryMode.doc: Shared memory related attributes for use with ::cuLaunchKernelEx.

cudaSharedMemoryModeDefault.doc: The default to use for allowing non-portable shared memory size on launch - uses current function attributes for [cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggac6c537b33d22c871a103f0fda8ac8bbea9d5a5aea324596d0e686f7c416f71c26).

cudaSharedMemoryModeRequirePortable.doc: Specifies that the shared memory size requested must be a portable size within [cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlock](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cdacf1490f9974e877131048b1b3eb8bdcc).

cudaSharedMemoryModeAllowNonPortable.doc: Specifies that the shared memory size requested may be a non-portable size up to [cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda024f669ca60d8ff7b3126dbfc61fd925).

cudaSharedMemoryModeAllowOversizedShared.doc: Specifies that oversized shared memory configurations may be used (with the limitation of only 8kB L1 cache).

cudaSharedMemoryModePreferOversizedShare.doc: Specifies that oversized shared memory configurations may be used (with the limitation of only 8kB L1 cache), and prefer an oversized shared memory configuration.

cudaStreamCaptureMode.doc:
Possible modes for stream capture thread interactions.

For more details see [cudaStreamBeginCapture](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1ga793d7d4e474388ddfda531603dc34aa3) and [cudaThreadExchangeStreamCaptureMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1ga9d0535d93a214cbf126835257b16ba85).

cudaStreamCaptureStatus.doc: Possible stream capture statuses returned by [cudaStreamIsCapturing](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1gae564e8434c67d716367931c4bc7db1cc).

cudaStreamCaptureStatusInvalidated.doc: Stream is part of a capture sequence that has been invalidated, but not terminated.

cudaStreamAddCaptureDependencies.doc: Add new nodes to the dependency set.

cudaStreamSetCaptureDependencies.doc: Replace the dependency set with the new nodes.

cudaReadModeElementType.doc: Read texture as specified element type.

cudaUserObjectFlags.doc: Flags for user objects for graphs.

cudaUserObjectNoDestructorSync.doc: Indicates the destructor execution is not synchronized by any CUDA handle.

cudaUserObjectRetainFlags.doc: Flags for retaining user object references for graphs.

cudaGraphUserObjectMove.doc: Transfer references from the caller rather than creating new references.

cudaDevResourceDesc_t.doc:
An opaque descriptor handle.

The descriptor encapsulates multiple created and configured resources. Created via ::cudaDeviceResourceGenerateDesc.

cudaExecutionContext_t.doc:
An opaque handle to a CUDA execution context.

It represents an execution context created via CUDA Runtime APIs such as [cudaGreenCtxCreate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION__CONTEXT.html#group__cudart__execution__context_1ga382a6e584f1e94865254f90080ff8f2c).

cudaGraphConditionalHandle.doc: CUDA handle for conditional graph nodes.

cudaGraphDeviceNode_t.doc: CUDA device node handle for device-side node update.

fields.Param userData: Argument value passed to the function

cudaSurfaceObject_t.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA Surface object.

cudaTextureObject_t.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA texture object.

cudaChooseDevice.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaChooseDevice(int * device, const struct cudaDeviceProp * prop)
cudaChooseDevice.doc:
Select compute-device which best matches criteria.

Returns in `*device` the device which has properties that best match `*prop`.

device.doc: Device with best match.

cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites(enum cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesTarget target, enum cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesScope scope)
cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites.doc:
Blocks until remote writes are visible to the specified scope.

Blocks until remote writes to the target context via mappings created through GPUDirect RDMA APIs, like nvidia_p2p_get_pages (see <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/gpudirect-rdma> for more information), are visible to the specified scope.

If the scope equals or lies within the scope indicated by [cudaDevAttrGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrdering](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda881d5b0c5bf7777e382920af4d743bde), the call will be a no-op and can be safely omitted for performance. This can be determined by comparing the numerical values between the two enums, with smaller scopes having smaller values.

Users may query support for this API via [cudaDevAttrGPUDirectRDMAFlushWritesOptions](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda7b3462e13705248606f39fb5381446ee).

target.doc: The target of the operation, see cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesTarget.

scope.doc: The scope of the operation, see cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesScope.

cudaDeviceGetAttribute.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetAttribute(int * value, enum cudaDeviceAttr attr, int device)
cudaDeviceGetAttribute.doc:
Returns information about the device.

Returns in `*value` the integer value of the attribute `attr` on device `device`.

value.doc: Returned device attribute value.

device.doc: Device number to query.

cudaDeviceGetByPCIBusId.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetByPCIBusId(int * device, const char * pciBusId)
cudaDeviceGetByPCIBusId.doc:
Returns a handle to a compute device.

Returns in `*device` a device ordinal given a PCI bus ID string.

where `domain`, `bus`, `device`, and `function` are all hexadecimal values.

device.doc: Returned device ordinal.

pciBusId.doc: String in one of the following forms.

cudaDeviceGetCacheConfig.doc:
Returns the preferred cache configuration for the current device.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this returns through `pCacheConfig` the preferred cache configuration for the current device. This is only a preference. The runtime will use the requested configuration if possible, but it is free to choose a different configuration if required to execute functions.

This will return a `pCacheConfig` of [cudaFuncCachePreferNone](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggab980f35ed69ee7991704de29a13de49ba3b4b8c65376ce1ca107be413e15981bc) on devices where the size of the L1 cache and shared memory are fixed.

The supported cache configurations are.

cudaDeviceGetDefaultMemPool.doc:
Returns the default mempool of a device.

The default mempool of a device contains device memory from that device.

cudaDeviceGetHostAtomicCapabilities.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetHostAtomicCapabilities(unsigned int * capabilities, const enum cudaAtomicOperation * operations, unsigned int count, int device)
cudaDeviceGetHostAtomicCapabilities.doc:
Queries details about atomic operations supported between the device and host.

Returns in `*capabilities` the details about requested atomic `*operations` over the link between `dev` and the host. The allocated size of `*operations` and `*capabilities` must be `count`.

For each [cudaAtomicOperation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga097391b0c5ed60f698c6b5d729b901fc) in `*operations`, the corresponding result in `*capabilities` will be a bitmask indicating which of [cudaAtomicOperationCapability](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga3ded8497f09d41455ea64acb7a880868) the link supports natively.

Returns [cudaErrorInvalidDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a938c6e8b96ecde62e3ab5137156f739a) if `dev` is not valid.

Returns [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) if `*capabilities` or `*operations` is NULL, if `count` is 0, or if any of `*operations` is not valid.

capabilities.doc: Returned capability details of each requested operation.

count.doc: Count of requested operations and size of capabilities.

cudaDeviceGetLimit.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetLimit(size_t * pValue, enum cudaLimit limit)
cudaDeviceGetLimit.doc:
Return resource limits.

Returns in `*pValue` the current size of `limit`. The following [cudaLimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651) values are supported.

cudaDeviceGetMemPool.doc:
Gets the current mempool for a device.

Returns the last pool provided to [cudaDeviceSetMemPool](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga02bb50d2e2af83e5f24d0b2ab9dadc82) for this device or the device’s default memory pool if [cudaDeviceSetMemPool](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga02bb50d2e2af83e5f24d0b2ab9dadc82) has never been called. By default the current mempool is the default mempool for a device, otherwise the returned pool must have been set with ::cuDeviceSetMemPool or [cudaDeviceSetMemPool](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga02bb50d2e2af83e5f24d0b2ab9dadc82).

cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes(void * nvSciSyncAttrList, int device, int flags)
cudaDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes.doc:
Return NvSciSync attributes that this device can support.

Returns in `nvSciSyncAttrList`, the properties of NvSciSync that this CUDA device, `dev` can support. The returned `nvSciSyncAttrList` can be used to create an NvSciSync that matches this device’s capabilities.

If NvSciSyncAttrKey_RequiredPerm field in `nvSciSyncAttrList` is already set this API will return [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c).

The applications should set `nvSciSyncAttrList` to a valid NvSciSyncAttrList failing which this API will return ::cudaErrorInvalidHandle.

The `flags` controls how applications intends to use the NvSciSync created from the `nvSciSyncAttrList`. The valid flags are:

At least one of these flags must be set, failing which the API returns [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c). Both the flags are orthogonal to one another: a developer may set both these flags that allows to set both wait and signal specific attributes in the same `nvSciSyncAttrList`.

Note that this API updates the input `nvSciSyncAttrList` with values equivalent to the following public attribute key-values: NvSciSyncAttrKey_RequiredPerm is set to

[cudaSuccess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ae355f04607d824883b4a50662830d591), [cudaErrorDeviceUninitialized](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a9e95927732f0d5a68151c72296581504), [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c), ::cudaErrorInvalidHandle, [cudaErrorInvalidDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a938c6e8b96ecde62e3ab5137156f739a), [cudaErrorNotSupported](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ad846fd9f2e8ba5e2fb4f1695b7ab6164), [cudaErrorMemoryAllocation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038af210f50ae7f17f655e0504929606add9).

device.doc: Valid CUDA Device to get NvSciSync attributes for.

cudaDeviceGetP2PAtomicCapabilities.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetP2PAtomicCapabilities(unsigned int * capabilities, const enum cudaAtomicOperation * operations, unsigned int count, int srcDevice, int dstDevice)
cudaDeviceGetP2PAtomicCapabilities.doc:
Queries details about atomic operations supported between two devices.

Returns in `*capabilities` the details about requested atomic `*operations` over the link between `srcDevice` and `dstDevice`. The allocated size of `*operations` and `*capabilities` must be `count`.

For each [cudaAtomicOperation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga097391b0c5ed60f698c6b5d729b901fc) in `*operations`, the corresponding result in `*capabilities` will be a bitmask indicating which of [cudaAtomicOperationCapability](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga3ded8497f09d41455ea64acb7a880868) the link supports natively.

Returns [cudaErrorInvalidDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a938c6e8b96ecde62e3ab5137156f739a) if `srcDevice` or `dstDevice` are not valid or if they represent the same device.

Returns [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) if `*capabilities` or `*operations` is NULL, if `count` is 0, or if any of `*operations` is not valid.

capabilities.doc: Returned capability details of each requested operation.

count.doc: Count of requested operations and size of capabilities.

srcDevice.doc: The source device of the target link.

dstDevice.doc: The destination device of the target link.

cudaDeviceGetP2PAttribute.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetP2PAttribute(int * value, enum cudaDeviceP2PAttr attr, int srcDevice, int dstDevice)
cudaDeviceGetP2PAttribute.doc:
Queries attributes of the link between two devices.

Returns in `*value` the value of the requested attribute `attrib` of the link between `srcDevice` and `dstDevice`. The supported attributes are:

Returns [cudaErrorInvalidDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a938c6e8b96ecde62e3ab5137156f739a) if `srcDevice` or `dstDevice` are not valid or if they represent the same device.

Returns [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) if `attrib` is not valid or if `value` is a null pointer.

value.doc: Returned value of the requested attribute.

attrib.doc: The requested attribute of the link between `srcDevice` and `dstDevice`.

srcDevice.doc: The source device of the target link.

dstDevice.doc: The destination device of the target link.

cudaDeviceGetPCIBusId.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetPCIBusId(char * pciBusId, int len, int device)
cudaDeviceGetPCIBusId.doc:
Returns a PCI Bus Id string for the device.

Returns an ASCII string identifying the device `dev` in the NULL-terminated string pointed to by `pciBusId`. `len` specifies the maximum length of the string that may be returned.

where `domain`, `bus`, `device`, and `function` are all hexadecimal values. pciBusId should be large enough to store 13 characters including the NULL-terminator.

pciBusId.doc: Returned identifier string for the device in the following format.

len.doc: Maximum length of string to store in `name`.

device.doc: Device to get identifier string for.

cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange.doc:
Returns numerical values that correspond to the least and greatest stream priorities.

Returns in `*leastPriority` and `*greatestPriority` the numerical values that correspond to the least and greatest stream priorities respectively. Stream priorities follow a convention where lower numbers imply greater priorities. The range of meaningful stream priorities is given by [`*greatestPriority`, `*leastPriority`]. If the user attempts to create a stream with a priority value that is outside the meaningful range as specified by this API, the priority is automatically clamped down or up to either `*leastPriority` or `*greatestPriority` respectively. See [cudaStreamCreateWithPriority](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1gae2be9e9858849bf62ba4a8b66d1c3540) for details on creating a priority stream. A NULL may be passed in for `*leastPriority` or `*greatestPriority` if the value is not desired.

This function will return ‘0’ in both `*leastPriority` and `*greatestPriority` if the current context’s device does not support stream priorities (see [cudaDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3559b8cc346511d423b5a6def5fbd3e0)).

leastPriority.doc: Pointer to an int in which the numerical value for least stream priority is returned.

greatestPriority.doc: Pointer to an int in which the numerical value for greatest stream priority is returned.

cudaDeviceGetTexture1DLinearMaxWidth.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetTexture1DLinearMaxWidth(size_t * maxWidthInElements, const struct cudaChannelFormatDesc * fmtDesc, int device)
cudaDeviceGetTexture1DLinearMaxWidth.doc:
Returns the maximum number of elements allocatable in a 1D linear texture for a given element size.

Returns in `maxWidthInElements` the maximum number of elements allocatable in a 1D linear texture for given format descriptor `fmtDesc`.

maxWidthInElements.doc: Returns maximum number of texture elements allocatable for given `fmtDesc`.

cudaDeviceRegisterAsyncNotification.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceRegisterAsyncNotification(int device, cudaAsyncCallback callbackFunc, void * userData, cudaAsyncCallbackHandle_t * callback)
cudaDeviceRegisterAsyncNotification.doc:
Registers a callback function to receive async notifications.

Registers `callbackFunc` to receive async notifications.

The `userData` parameter is passed to the callback function at async notification time. Likewise, `callback` is also passed to the callback function to distinguish between multiple registered callbacks.

The callback function being registered should be designed to return quickly (~10ms). Any long running tasks should be queued for execution on an application thread.

Callbacks may not call cudaDeviceRegisterAsyncNotification or cudaDeviceUnregisterAsyncNotification. Doing so will result in [cudaErrorNotPermitted](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a67b6095ab719b21659a400b553963eb3). Async notification callbacks execute in an undefined order and may be serialized.

Returns in `*callback` a handle representing the registered callback instance.

device.doc: The device on which to register the callback.

callbackFunc.doc: The function to register as a callback.

userData.doc: A generic pointer to user data. This is passed into the callback function.

callback.doc: A handle representing the registered callback instance.

cudaDeviceReset.doc:
Destroy all allocations and reset all state on the current device in the current process.

Explicitly destroys and cleans up all resources associated with the current device in the current process. It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure that the resources are not accessed or passed in subsequent API calls and doing so will result in undefined behavior. These resources include CUDA types [cudaStream_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gae15d9c8b7a240312b533d6122558085a), [cudaEvent_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaea2f543a9fc0e52fe4ae712920fd1247), [cudaArray_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaaf8b3ba752727d996074a71ee997ce68), [cudaMipmappedArray_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga1b03ad14fc0ab86f8b033837f5562d8a), [cudaPitchedPtr](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaPitchedPtr.html#structcudapitchedptr), [cudaTextureObject_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga83eb271ebc4cb2817e66d7c752f0c29b), [cudaSurfaceObject_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gabe57cf2ccbe7f9d696f18808dd634c0a), ::textureReference, ::surfaceReference, [cudaExternalMemory_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga79a2bf6a3a2aa9011a96dc17d476faf7), [cudaExternalSemaphore_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaf8bc7ab93d638c5835e5289ac7d683c4) and [cudaGraphicsResource_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaf58dd8d3c7a65714ff7f5459adbf7e6f). These resources also include memory allocations by [cudaMalloc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae63c9974e34b14fd750efd91b32f405b), [cudaMallocHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gaab84100ae1fa1b12eaca660207ef585b), [cudaMallocManaged](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gaec54cd99121bfb36af81257463b5cb81) and [cudaMallocPitch](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga32bd7a39135594788a542ae72217775c). Any subsequent API call to this device will reinitialize the device.

Note that this function will reset the device immediately. It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure that the device is not being accessed by any other host threads from the process when this function is called.

cudaDeviceSetCacheConfig.doc:
Sets the preferred cache configuration for the current device.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this sets through `cacheConfig` the preferred cache configuration for the current device. This is only a preference. The runtime will use the requested configuration if possible, but it is free to choose a different configuration if required to execute the function. Any function preference set via [cudaFuncSetCacheConfig (C API)](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga6699ca1943ac2655effa0d571b2f4f15) or [cudaFuncSetCacheConfig (C++ API)](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__HIGHLEVEL.html#group__cudart__highlevel_1ga981c8d74d33b21e7fd57609b7337653e) will be preferred over this device-wide setting. Setting the device-wide cache configuration to [cudaFuncCachePreferNone](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggab980f35ed69ee7991704de29a13de49ba3b4b8c65376ce1ca107be413e15981bc) will cause subsequent kernel launches to prefer to not change the cache configuration unless required to launch the kernel.

This setting does nothing on devices where the size of the L1 cache and shared memory are fixed.

Launching a kernel with a different preference than the most recent preference setting may insert a device-side synchronization point.

The supported cache configurations are.

cudaDeviceSetLimit.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaDeviceSetLimit(enum cudaLimit limit, size_t value)
cudaDeviceSetLimit.doc:
Set resource limits.

Setting `limit` to `value` is a request by the application to update the current limit maintained by the device. The driver is free to modify the requested value to meet h/w requirements (this could be clamping to minimum or maximum values, rounding up to nearest element size, etc). The application can use [cudaDeviceGetLimit()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga00404a8f3343448d28c47eea954163a1) to find out exactly what the limit has been set to.

Setting each [cudaLimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651) has its own specific restrictions, so each is discussed here.

value.doc: Size of limit.

cudaDeviceSetMemPool.doc:
Sets the current memory pool of a device.

The memory pool must be local to the specified device. Unless a mempool is specified in the [cudaMallocAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1gabbf70065888d61853c047513baa14081) call, [cudaMallocAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1gabbf70065888d61853c047513baa14081) allocates from the current mempool of the provided stream’s device. By default, a device’s current memory pool is its default memory pool.

cudaDeviceSynchronize.doc:
Wait for compute device to finish.

Blocks until the device has completed all preceding requested tasks. [cudaDeviceSynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga096cfe1b3923b1932ef4af405ec7c1b9) returns an error if one of the preceding tasks has failed. If the [cudaDeviceScheduleBlockingSync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga057e6912c52708b6aa86e79dd83d007c) flag was set for this device, the host thread will block until the device has finished its work.

cudaDeviceUnregisterAsyncNotification.doc:
Unregisters an async notification callback.

Unregisters `callback` so that the corresponding callback function will stop receiving async notifications.

device.doc: The device from which to remove `callback`.

callback.doc: The callback instance to unregister from receiving async notifications.

cudaGetDevice.doc:
Returns which device is currently being used.

Returns in `*device` the current device for the calling host thread.

cudaGetDeviceCount.doc:
Returns the number of compute-capable devices.

Returns in `*count` the number of devices with compute capability greater or equal to 2.0 that are available for execution.

cudaGetDeviceFlags.doc:
Gets the flags for the current device.

Returns in `flags` the flags for the current device. If there is a current device for the calling thread, the flags for the device are returned. If there is no current device, the flags for the first device are returned, which may be the default flags. Compare to the behavior of [cudaSetDeviceFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga69e73c7dda3fc05306ae7c811a690fac).

Typically, the flags returned should match the behavior that will be seen if the calling thread uses a device after this call, without any change to the flags or current device inbetween by this or another thread. Note that if the device is not initialized, it is possible for another thread to change the flags for the current device before it is initialized. Additionally, when using exclusive mode, if this thread has not requested a specific device, it may use a device other than the first device, contrary to the assumption made by this function.

If a context has been created via the driver API and is current to the calling thread, the flags for that context are always returned.

Flags returned by this function may specifically include [cudaDeviceMapHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga3762be9cccdd809a4ca128354fd134b0) even though it is not accepted by [cudaSetDeviceFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga69e73c7dda3fc05306ae7c811a690fac) because it is implicit in runtime API flags. The reason for this is that the current context may have been created via the driver API in which case the flag is not implicit and may be unset.

cudaGetDeviceProperties.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGetDeviceProperties(struct cudaDeviceProp * prop, int device)
cudaGetDeviceProperties.doc:
Returns information about the compute-device.

Returns in `*prop` the properties of device `dev`.

device.doc: Device number to get properties for.

cudaInitDevice.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaInitDevice(int device, unsigned int deviceFlags, unsigned int flags)
cudaInitDevice.doc:
Initialize device to be used for GPU executions.

This function will initialize the CUDA Runtime structures and primary context on `device` when called, but the context will not be made current to `device`.

When [cudaInitDeviceFlagsAreValid](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga2ff861a477ec064dcf01977194158e49) is set in `flags`, deviceFlags are applied to the requested device. The values of deviceFlags match those of the flags parameters in [cudaSetDeviceFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga69e73c7dda3fc05306ae7c811a690fac). The effect may be verified by [cudaGetDeviceFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1gaf830794caf068b71638c6182bba8f77a).

This function will return an error if the device is in [cudaComputeModeExclusiveProcess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga7eb25f5413a962faad0956d92bae10d0a2cd032834fecbec513ea1018145b111d) and is occupied by another process or if the device is in [cudaComputeModeProhibited](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga7eb25f5413a962faad0956d92bae10d0afc71b88518e4501544d6e65b5f3671b6).

device.doc: Device on which the runtime will initialize itself.

flags.doc: Flags for controlling the device initialization.

cudaIpcCloseMemHandle.doc:
Attempts to close memory mapped with cudaIpcOpenMemHandle.

Decrements the reference count of the memory returnd by [cudaIpcOpenMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga01050a29fefde385b1042081ada4cde9) by 1. When the reference count reaches 0, this API unmaps the memory. The original allocation in the exporting process as well as imported mappings in other processes will be unaffected.

Any resources used to enable peer access will be freed if this is the last mapping using them.

IPC functionality is restricted to devices with support for unified addressing on Linux and Windows operating systems. IPC functionality on Windows is supported for compatibility purposes but not recommended as it comes with performance cost. Users can test their device for IPC functionality by calling [cudaDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3559b8cc346511d423b5a6def5fbd3e0) with [cudaDevAttrIpcEventSupport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda0ab012a7c597ffbe86090ee2f9e1758c).

cudaIpcGetEventHandle.doc:
Gets an interprocess handle for a previously allocated event.

Takes as input a previously allocated event. This event must have been created with the [cudaEventInterprocess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga49ec9cd742f8a3f6fde4ee72a66326f6) and [cudaEventDisableTiming](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaa5d3eff7c3623e2be533968d9cc1ee7e) flags set. This opaque handle may be copied into other processes and opened with [cudaIpcOpenEventHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga9691446ab0aec1d6e528357387ed87b2) to allow efficient hardware synchronization between GPU work in different processes.

After the event has been been opened in the importing process, [cudaEventRecord](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1gac9bd8aa1d0473f9b39460701d39a388a), [cudaEventSynchronize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1ga949aa42b30ae9e622f6ba0787129ff22), [cudaStreamWaitEvent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1gad55b210296a2ad78e8f663a4036e7804) and [cudaEventQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1ga2bf738909b4a059023537eaa29d8a5b7) may be used in either process. Performing operations on the imported event after the exported event has been freed with [cudaEventDestroy](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1gae42ae0a54561030bd4270f16d2a70716) will result in undefined behavior.

IPC functionality is restricted to devices with support for unified addressing on Linux and Windows operating systems. IPC functionality on Windows is supported for compatibility purposes but not recommended as it comes with performance cost. Users can test their device for IPC functionality by calling [cudaDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3559b8cc346511d423b5a6def5fbd3e0) with [cudaDevAttrIpcEventSupport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda0ab012a7c597ffbe86090ee2f9e1758c).

handle.doc: Pointer to a user allocated cudaIpcEventHandle in which to return the opaque event handle.

cudaIpcGetMemHandle.doc:
Gets an interprocess memory handle for an existing device memory allocation.

Takes a pointer to the base of an existing device memory allocation created with [cudaMalloc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae63c9974e34b14fd750efd91b32f405b) and exports it for use in another process. This is a lightweight operation and may be called multiple times on an allocation without adverse effects.

If a region of memory is freed with [cudaFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6) and a subsequent call to [cudaMalloc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae63c9974e34b14fd750efd91b32f405b) returns memory with the same device address, [cudaIpcGetMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga8a37f7dfafaca652391d0758b3667539) will return a unique handle for the new memory.

IPC functionality is restricted to devices with support for unified addressing on Linux and Windows operating systems. IPC functionality on Windows is supported for compatibility purposes but not recommended as it comes with performance cost. Users can test their device for IPC functionality by calling [cudaDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3559b8cc346511d423b5a6def5fbd3e0) with [cudaDevAttrIpcEventSupport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda0ab012a7c597ffbe86090ee2f9e1758c).

handle.doc: Pointer to user allocated ::cudaIpcMemHandle to return the handle in.

devPtr.doc: Base pointer to previously allocated device memory.

cudaIpcOpenEventHandle.doc:
Opens an interprocess event handle for use in the current process.

Opens an interprocess event handle exported from another process with [cudaIpcGetEventHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga89a3abe1e9a11d08c665176669109784). This function returns a [cudaEvent_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaea2f543a9fc0e52fe4ae712920fd1247) that behaves like a locally created event with the [cudaEventDisableTiming](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaa5d3eff7c3623e2be533968d9cc1ee7e) flag specified. This event must be freed with [cudaEventDestroy](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1gae42ae0a54561030bd4270f16d2a70716).

Performing operations on the imported event after the exported event has been freed with [cudaEventDestroy](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1gae42ae0a54561030bd4270f16d2a70716) will result in undefined behavior.

IPC functionality is restricted to devices with support for unified addressing on Linux and Windows operating systems. IPC functionality on Windows is supported for compatibility purposes but not recommended as it comes with performance cost. Users can test their device for IPC functionality by calling [cudaDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3559b8cc346511d423b5a6def5fbd3e0) with [cudaDevAttrIpcEventSupport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda0ab012a7c597ffbe86090ee2f9e1758c).

cudaIpcOpenMemHandle.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaIpcOpenMemHandle(void * * devPtr, cudaIpcMemHandle_t handle, unsigned int flags)
cudaIpcOpenMemHandle.doc:
Opens an interprocess memory handle exported from another process and returns a device pointer usable in the local process.

Maps memory exported from another process with [cudaIpcGetMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga8a37f7dfafaca652391d0758b3667539) into the current device address space. For contexts on different devices [cudaIpcOpenMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga01050a29fefde385b1042081ada4cde9) can attempt to enable peer access between the devices as if the user called [cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__PEER.html#group__cudart__peer_1ga2b0adabf90db37e5cfddc92cbb2589f3). This behavior is controlled by the [cudaIpcMemLazyEnablePeerAccess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga60f28a5142ee7ae0336dfa83fd54e006) flag. [cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__PEER.html#group__cudart__peer_1ga4db0d04e44995d5c1c34be4ecc863f22) can determine if a mapping is possible.

[cudaIpcOpenMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga01050a29fefde385b1042081ada4cde9) can open handles to devices that may not be visible in the process calling the API.

Contexts that may open ::cudaIpcMemHandles are restricted in the following way. ::cudaIpcMemHandles from each device in a given process may only be opened by one context per device per other process.

If the memory handle has already been opened by the current context, the reference count on the handle is incremented by 1 and the existing device pointer is returned.

Memory returned from [cudaIpcOpenMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga01050a29fefde385b1042081ada4cde9) must be freed with [cudaIpcCloseMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga02bb3632b5d223db6acae5f8744e2c91).

Calling [cudaFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6) on an exported memory region before calling [cudaIpcCloseMemHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga02bb3632b5d223db6acae5f8744e2c91) in the importing context will result in undefined behavior.

IPC functionality is restricted to devices with support for unified addressing on Linux and Windows operating systems. IPC functionality on Windows is supported for compatibility purposes but not recommended as it comes with performance cost. Users can test their device for IPC functionality by calling [cudaDeviceGetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3559b8cc346511d423b5a6def5fbd3e0) with [cudaDevAttrIpcEventSupport](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda0ab012a7c597ffbe86090ee2f9e1758c).

devPtr.doc: Returned device pointer.

flags.doc: Flags for this operation. Must be specified as [cudaIpcMemLazyEnablePeerAccess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga60f28a5142ee7ae0336dfa83fd54e006).

cudaSetDevice.doc:
Set device to be used for GPU executions.

Sets `device` as the current device for the calling host thread. Valid device id’s are 0 to ([cudaGetDeviceCount()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1gaf639fa9dfe6f65432869c52b5797f8ce) - 1).

Any device memory subsequently allocated from this host thread using [cudaMalloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae63c9974e34b14fd750efd91b32f405b), [cudaMallocPitch()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga32bd7a39135594788a542ae72217775c) or [cudaMallocArray()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga6728eb7dc25f332f50bdb16a19620d3d) will be physically resident on `device`. Any host memory allocated from this host thread using [cudaMallocHost()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gaab84100ae1fa1b12eaca660207ef585b) or [cudaHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gab65da58f444e7230d3322b6126bb4902) or [cudaHostRegister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae8d5c17670f16ac4fc8fcb4181cb490c) will have its lifetime associated with `device`. Any streams or events created from this host thread will be associated with `device`. Any kernels launched from this host thread using the <<<>>> operator or [cudaLaunchKernel()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga5064cdf5d8e6741ace56fd8be951783c) will be executed on `device`.

This call may be made from any host thread, to any device, and at any time. This function will do no synchronization with the previous or new device, and should only take significant time when it initializes the runtime’s context state. This call will bind the primary context of the specified device to the calling thread and all the subsequent memory allocations, stream and event creations, and kernel launches will be associated with the primary context. This function will also immediately initialize the runtime state on the primary context, and the context will be current on `device` immediately. This function will return an error if the device is in [cudaComputeModeExclusiveProcess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga7eb25f5413a962faad0956d92bae10d0a2cd032834fecbec513ea1018145b111d) and is occupied by another process or if the device is in [cudaComputeModeProhibited](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga7eb25f5413a962faad0956d92bae10d0afc71b88518e4501544d6e65b5f3671b6).

It is not required to call [cudaInitDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1gaac04a5d82168676b20121ca870919419) before using this function.

cudaSetDeviceFlags.doc:
Sets flags to be used for device executions.

Records `flags` as the flags for the current device. If the current device has been set and that device has already been initialized, the previous flags are overwritten. If the current device has not been initialized, it is initialized with the provided flags. If no device has been made current to the calling thread, a default device is selected and initialized with the provided flags.

The three LSBs of the `flags` parameter can be used to control how the CPU thread interacts with the OS scheduler when waiting for results from the device.

cudaSetValidDevices.doc:
Set a list of devices that can be used for CUDA.

Sets a list of devices for CUDA execution in priority order using `device_arr`. The parameter `len` specifies the number of elements in the list. CUDA will try devices from the list sequentially until it finds one that works. If this function is not called, or if it is called with a `len` of 0, then CUDA will go back to its default behavior of trying devices sequentially from a default list containing all of the available CUDA devices in the system. If a specified device ID in the list does not exist, this function will return [cudaErrorInvalidDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a938c6e8b96ecde62e3ab5137156f739a). If `len` is not 0 and `device_arr` is NULL or if `len` exceeds the number of devices in the system, then [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) is returned.

len.doc: Number of devices in specified list.

cudaDeviceGetSharedMemConfig.doc:
Returns the shared memory configuration for the current device.

This function will return in `pConfig` the current size of shared memory banks on the current device. On devices with configurable shared memory banks, [cudaDeviceSetSharedMemConfig](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__device__deprecated_1gaa4f3f8a422968f9524012f43ba852058) can be used to change this setting, so that all subsequent kernel launches will by default use the new bank size. When [cudaDeviceGetSharedMemConfig](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__device__deprecated_1gafb2038893286a743347dada716bab162) is called on devices without configurable shared memory, it will return the fixed bank size of the hardware.

The returned bank configurations can be either.

cudaDeviceSetSharedMemConfig.doc:
Sets the shared memory configuration for the current device.

On devices with configurable shared memory banks, this function will set the shared memory bank size which is used for all subsequent kernel launches. Any per-function setting of shared memory set via [cudaFuncSetSharedMemConfig](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__execution__deprecated_1ga3ef735b45b7549e936a60cb084740754) will override the device wide setting.

Changing the shared memory configuration between launches may introduce a device side synchronization point.

Changing the shared memory bank size will not increase shared memory usage or affect occupancy of kernels, but may have major effects on performance. Larger bank sizes will allow for greater potential bandwidth to shared memory, but will change what kinds of accesses to shared memory will result in bank conflicts.

This function will do nothing on devices with fixed shared memory bank size.

The supported bank configurations are.

cudaD3D10DeviceList.doc: CUDA devices corresponding to a D3D10 device.

cudaD3D10DeviceListAll.doc: The CUDA devices for all GPUs used by a D3D10 device.

cudaD3D10DeviceListCurrentFrame.doc: The CUDA devices for the GPUs used by a D3D10 device in its currently rendering frame.

cudaD3D10DeviceListNextFrame.doc: The CUDA devices for the GPUs to be used by a D3D10 device in the next frame.

cudaD3D10GetDevice.doc:
Gets the device number for an adapter.

Returns in `*device` the CUDA-compatible device corresponding to the adapter `pAdapter` obtained from ::IDXGIFactory::EnumAdapters. This call will succeed only if a device on adapter `pAdapter` is CUDA-compatible.

device.doc: Returns the device corresponding to pAdapter.

pAdapter.doc: D3D10 adapter to get device for.

cudaD3D10GetDevices.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaD3D10GetDevices(unsigned int * pCudaDeviceCount, int * pCudaDevices, unsigned int cudaDeviceCount, ID3D10Device * pD3D10Device, enum cudaD3D10DeviceList deviceList)
cudaD3D10GetDevices.doc:
Gets the CUDA devices corresponding to a Direct3D 10 device.

Returns in `*pCudaDeviceCount` the number of CUDA-compatible devices corresponding to the Direct3D 10 device `pD3D10Device`. Also returns in `*pCudaDevices` at most `cudaDeviceCount` of the CUDA-compatible devices corresponding to the Direct3D 10 device `pD3D10Device`.

If any of the GPUs being used to render `pDevice` are not CUDA capable then the call will return [cudaErrorNoDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ae942e4cbbd2bef6e92e293253f055613).

pCudaDeviceCount.doc: Returned number of CUDA devices corresponding to `pD3D10Device`.

cudaDeviceCount.doc: The size of the output device array `pCudaDevices`.

pD3D10Device.doc: Direct3D 10 device to query for CUDA devices.

deviceList.doc: The set of devices to return. This set may be [cudaD3D10DeviceListAll](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D10.html#group__cudart__d3d10_1gga1e9ffdd1c631cab046c7d7b64e187f78ae91df6bb0bf994be807d0acec5694f30) for all devices, [cudaD3D10DeviceListCurrentFrame](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D10.html#group__cudart__d3d10_1gga1e9ffdd1c631cab046c7d7b64e187f78a141da82f40280c96160f2346d1616699) for the devices used to render the current frame (in SLI), or [cudaD3D10DeviceListNextFrame](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D10.html#group__cudart__d3d10_1gga1e9ffdd1c631cab046c7d7b64e187f78ab9214ae4b1b2c1899b980071c20a65ba) for the devices used to render the next frame (in SLI).

cudaGraphicsD3D10RegisterResource.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphicsD3D10RegisterResource(struct cudaGraphicsResource * * resource, ID3D10Resource * pD3DResource, unsigned int flags)
cudaGraphicsD3D10RegisterResource.doc:
Registers a Direct3D 10 resource for access by CUDA.

Registers the Direct3D 10 resource `pD3DResource` for access by CUDA.

If this call is successful, then the application will be able to map and unmap this resource until it is unregistered through [cudaGraphicsUnregisterResource()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__INTEROP.html#group__cudart__interop_1gac65d1f2900086747de1e57301d709940). Also on success, this call will increase the internal reference count on `pD3DResource`. This reference count will be decremented when this resource is unregistered through [cudaGraphicsUnregisterResource()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__INTEROP.html#group__cudart__interop_1gac65d1f2900086747de1e57301d709940).

This call potentially has a high-overhead and should not be called every frame in interactive applications.

The type of `pD3DResource` must be one of the following.

The `flags` argument may be used to specify additional parameters at register time. The valid values for this parameter are

Not all Direct3D resources of the above types may be used for interoperability with CUDA. The following are some limitations.

A complete list of supported DXGI formats is as follows. For compactness the notation A_{B,C,D} represents A_B, A_C, and A_D.

If `pD3DResource` is of incorrect type or is already registered, then [cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ac4673247aee4d1ab8d07871f376e0273) is returned. If `pD3DResource` cannot be registered, then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

cudaD3D10MapFlagsNone.doc: Default; Assume resource can be read/written.

cudaD3D10MapFlagsReadOnly.doc: CUDA kernels will not write to this resource.

cudaD3D10MapFlagsWriteDiscard.doc: CUDA kernels will only write to and will not read from this resource.

cudaD3D10RegisterFlagsNone.doc: Default; Resource can be accessed through a void\*.

cudaD3D10RegisterFlagsArray.doc: Resource can be accessed through a CUarray\*.

cudaD3D10GetDirect3DDevice.doc: Gets the Direct3D device against which the current CUDA context was created.

cudaD3D10MapResources.doc:
Maps Direct3D Resources for access by CUDA.

Maps the `count` Direct3D resources in `ppResources` for access by CUDA.

The resources in `ppResources` may be accessed in CUDA kernels until they are unmapped. Direct3D should not access any resources while they are mapped by CUDA. If an application does so, the results are undefined.

This function provides the synchronization guarantee that any Direct3D calls issued before [cudaD3D10MapResources()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D10__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__d3d10__deprecated_1ga6c4e7c5d77b0adf3882649cfe97d6790) will complete before any CUDA kernels issued after [cudaD3D10MapResources()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D10__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__d3d10__deprecated_1ga6c4e7c5d77b0adf3882649cfe97d6790) begin.

If any of `ppResources` have not been registered for use with CUDA or if `ppResources` contains any duplicate entries then [cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ac4673247aee4d1ab8d07871f376e0273) is returned. If any of `ppResources` are presently mapped for access by CUDA then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

count.doc: Number of resources to map for CUDA.
