cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdatesApply.signature: __device__ cudaError_t cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdatesApply(const cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdate * updates, size_t updateCount)
cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdatesApply.doc:
Batch applies multiple kernel node updates.

Batch applies one or more kernel node updates based on the information provided in `updates`. `updateCount` specifies the number of updates to apply. Each entry in `updates` must specify a node to update, the type of update to apply, and the parameters for that type of update. See the documentation for [cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdate](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaGraphKernelNodeUpdate.html#structcudagraphkernelnodeupdate) for more detail.

If this function is called for the node’s immediate dependent and that dependent is configured for programmatic dependent launch, then a memory fence must be invoked via __threadfence() before kickoff of the dependent is triggered via [cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1gae194af462d927583bed3acf60d450218) to ensure that the update is visible to that dependent node before it is launched.

updateCount.doc: The number of updates to apply.

cudaGraphLaunch.doc:
Launches an executable graph in a stream.

Executes `graphExec` in `stream`. Only one instance of `graphExec` may be executing at a time. Each launch is ordered behind both any previous work in `stream` and any previous launches of `graphExec`. To execute a graph concurrently, it must be instantiated multiple times into multiple executable graphs.

If any allocations created by `graphExec` remain unfreed (from a previous launch) and `graphExec` was not instantiated with [cudaGraphInstantiateFlagAutoFreeOnLaunch](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga638577f2b0f6a98b5e6a0e6a72d09004a4258c8d3adc203f97e73e92810e1785f), the launch will fail with [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c).

stream.doc: Stream in which to launch the graph.

cudaGraphMemAllocNodeGetParams.doc:
Returns a memory alloc node’s parameters.

Returns the parameters of a memory alloc node `hNode` in `params_out`. The `poolProps` and `accessDescs` returned in `params_out`, are owned by the node. This memory remains valid until the node is destroyed. The returned parameters must not be modified.

node.doc: Node to get the parameters for.

cudaGraphMemFreeNodeGetParams.doc:
Returns a memory free node’s parameters.

Returns the address of a memory free node `hNode` in `dptr_out`.

node.doc: Node to get the parameters for.

dptr_out.doc: Pointer to return the device address.

cudaGraphMemcpyNodeGetParams.doc:
Returns a memcpy node’s parameters.

Returns the parameters of memcpy node `node` in `pNodeParams`.

node.doc: Node to get the parameters for.

cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParams.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParams(cudaGraphNode_t node, const struct cudaMemcpy3DParms * pNodeParams)
cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParams.doc:
Sets a memcpy node’s parameters.

Sets the parameters of memcpy node `node` to `pNodeParams`.

node.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParams1D.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParams1D(cudaGraphNode_t node, void * dst, const void * src, size_t count, enum cudaMemcpyKind kind)
cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParams1D.doc:
Sets a memcpy node’s parameters to perform a 1-dimensional copy.

Sets the parameters of memcpy node `node` to the copy described by the provided parameters.

When the graph is launched, the node will copy `count` bytes from the memory area pointed to by `src` to the memory area pointed to by `dst`, where `kind` specifies the direction of the copy, and must be one of [cudaMemcpyHostToHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95badeec295de8a74ac2a74f98ffb6c5d7c7), [cudaMemcpyHostToDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba1a03d03a676ea8ec51b9b1e193617568), [cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba5653197602d3455a530db5a7edb1a253), [cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba783338534304281650c6cb1363f5a00a), or [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a). Passing [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a) is recommended, in which case the type of transfer is inferred from the pointer values. However, [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a) is only allowed on systems that support unified virtual addressing. Launching a memcpy node with dst and src pointers that do not match the direction of the copy results in an undefined behavior.

node.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParamsFromSymbol.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParamsFromSymbol(cudaGraphNode_t node, void * dst, const void * symbol, size_t count, size_t offset, enum cudaMemcpyKind kind)
cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParamsFromSymbol.doc:
Sets a memcpy node’s parameters to copy from a symbol on the device.

Sets the parameters of memcpy node `node` to the copy described by the provided parameters.

When the graph is launched, the node will copy `count` bytes from the memory area pointed to by `offset` bytes from the start of symbol `symbol` to the memory area pointed to by `dst`. The memory areas may not overlap. `symbol` is a variable that resides in global or constant memory space. `kind` can be either [cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba5653197602d3455a530db5a7edb1a253), [cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba783338534304281650c6cb1363f5a00a), or [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a). Passing [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a) is recommended, in which case the type of transfer is inferred from the pointer values. However, [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a) is only allowed on systems that support unified virtual addressing.

node.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

offset.doc: Offset from start of symbol in bytes.

cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParamsToSymbol.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParamsToSymbol(cudaGraphNode_t node, const void * symbol, const void * src, size_t count, size_t offset, enum cudaMemcpyKind kind)
cudaGraphMemcpyNodeSetParamsToSymbol.doc:
Sets a memcpy node’s parameters to copy to a symbol on the device.

Sets the parameters of memcpy node `node` to the copy described by the provided parameters.

When the graph is launched, the node will copy `count` bytes from the memory area pointed to by `src` to the memory area pointed to by `offset` bytes from the start of symbol `symbol`. The memory areas may not overlap. `symbol` is a variable that resides in global or constant memory space. `kind` can be either [cudaMemcpyHostToDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba1a03d03a676ea8ec51b9b1e193617568), [cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba783338534304281650c6cb1363f5a00a), or [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a). Passing [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a) is recommended, in which case the type of transfer is inferred from the pointer values. However, [cudaMemcpyDefault](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95ba715aff8fb2b8f4f1bb553fee802db57a) is only allowed on systems that support unified virtual addressing.

node.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

offset.doc: Offset from start of symbol in bytes.

cudaGraphMemsetNodeGetParams.doc:
Returns a memset node’s parameters.

Returns the parameters of memset node `node` in `pNodeParams`.

node.doc: Node to get the parameters for.

cudaGraphMemsetNodeSetParams.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphMemsetNodeSetParams(cudaGraphNode_t node, const struct cudaMemsetParams * pNodeParams)
cudaGraphMemsetNodeSetParams.doc:
Sets a memset node’s parameters.

Sets the parameters of memset node `node` to `pNodeParams`.

node.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

cudaGraphNodeFindInClone.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeFindInClone(cudaGraphNode_t * pNode, cudaGraphNode_t originalNode, cudaGraph_t clonedGraph)
cudaGraphNodeFindInClone.doc:
Finds a cloned version of a node.

This function returns the node in `clonedGraph` corresponding to `originalNode` in the original graph.

`clonedGraph` must have been cloned from `originalGraph` via [cudaGraphClone](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__cudart__graph_1ga711477355655f00773a0885fbf2891d6). `originalNode` must have been in `originalGraph` at the time of the call to [cudaGraphClone](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__cudart__graph_1ga711477355655f00773a0885fbf2891d6), and the corresponding cloned node in `clonedGraph` must not have been removed. The cloned node is then returned via `pClonedNode`.

pNode.doc: Returns handle to the cloned node.

cudaGraphNodeGetContainingGraph.doc:
Returns the graph that contains a given graph node.

Returns the graph that contains `hNode` in `*phGraph`. If hNode is in a child graph, the child graph it is in is returned.

phGraph.doc: Pointer to return the containing graph.

cudaGraphNodeGetDependencies.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetDependencies(cudaGraphNode_t node, cudaGraphNode_t * pDependencies, cudaGraphEdgeData * edgeData, size_t * pNumDependencies)
cudaGraphNodeGetDependencies.doc:
Returns a node’s dependencies.

Returns a list of `node's` dependencies. `pDependencies` may be NULL, in which case this function will return the number of dependencies in `pNumDependencies`. Otherwise, `pNumDependencies` entries will be filled in. If `pNumDependencies` is higher than the actual number of dependencies, the remaining entries in `pDependencies` will be set to NULL, and the number of nodes actually obtained will be returned in `pNumDependencies`.

Note that if an edge has non-zero (non-default) edge data and `edgeData` is NULL, this API will return [cudaErrorLossyQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ad484d9d8e8f269cf93d4c111b646f908). If `edgeData` is non-NULL, then `pDependencies` must be as well.

node.doc: Node to query.

edgeData.doc: Optional array to return edge data for each dependency.

cudaGraphNodeGetDependentNodes.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetDependentNodes(cudaGraphNode_t node, cudaGraphNode_t * pDependentNodes, cudaGraphEdgeData * edgeData, size_t * pNumDependentNodes)
cudaGraphNodeGetDependentNodes.doc:
Returns a node’s dependent nodes.

Returns a list of `node's` dependent nodes. `pDependentNodes` may be NULL, in which case this function will return the number of dependent nodes in `pNumDependentNodes`. Otherwise, `pNumDependentNodes` entries will be filled in. If `pNumDependentNodes` is higher than the actual number of dependent nodes, the remaining entries in `pDependentNodes` will be set to NULL, and the number of nodes actually obtained will be returned in `pNumDependentNodes`.

Note that if an edge has non-zero (non-default) edge data and `edgeData` is NULL, this API will return [cudaErrorLossyQuery](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ad484d9d8e8f269cf93d4c111b646f908). If `edgeData` is non-NULL, then `pDependentNodes` must be as well.

node.doc: Node to query.

pDependentNodes.doc: Pointer to return the dependent nodes.

edgeData.doc: Optional pointer to return edge data for dependent nodes.

cudaGraphNodeGetEnabled.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetEnabled(cudaGraphExec_t hGraphExec, cudaGraphNode_t hNode, unsigned int * isEnabled)
cudaGraphNodeGetEnabled.doc:
Query whether a node in the given graphExec is enabled.

Sets isEnabled to 1 if `hNode` is enabled, or 0 if `hNode` is disabled.

The node is identified by the corresponding node `hNode` in the non-executable graph, from which the executable graph was instantiated.

`hNode` must not have been removed from the original graph.

hGraphExec.doc: The executable graph in which to set the specified node.

hNode.doc: Node from the graph from which graphExec was instantiated.

isEnabled.doc: Location to return the enabled status of the node.

cudaGraphNodeGetLocalId.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetLocalId(cudaGraphNode_t hNode, unsigned int * nodeId)
cudaGraphNodeGetLocalId.doc:
Returns the node id of a given graph node.

Returns the node id of `hNode` in `*nodeId`. The nodeId matches that referenced by [cudaGraphDebugDotPrint](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__cudart__graph_1gabec177c250000405c570dc8c4bde20db). The local nodeId and graphId together can uniquely identify the node.

cudaGraphNodeGetParams.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetParams(cudaGraphNode_t node, struct cudaGraphNodeParams * nodeParams)
cudaGraphNodeGetParams.doc:
Returns a graph node’s parameters.

Returns the parameters of graph node `node` in `*nodeParams`.

Any pointers returned in `*nodeParams` point to driver-owned memory associated with the node. This memory remains valid until the node is destroyed. Any memory pointed to from `*nodeParams` must not be modified.

The returned parameters are a description of the node, but may not be identical to the struct provided at creation and may not be suitable for direct creation of identical nodes. This is because parameters may be partially unspecified and filled in by the driver at creation, may reference non-copyable handles, or may describe ownership semantics or other parameters that govern behavior of node creation but are not part of the final functional descriptor.

node.doc: Node to get the parameters for.

cudaGraphNodeGetToolsId.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetToolsId(cudaGraphNode_t hNode, unsigned long long * toolsNodeId)
cudaGraphNodeGetToolsId.doc: Returns an id used by tools to identify a given node.

\\*toolsNodeId.doc: Pointer to return the id used by tools.

cudaGraphNodeGetType.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeGetType(cudaGraphNode_t node, enum cudaGraphNodeType * pType)
cudaGraphNodeGetType.doc:
Returns a node’s type.

Returns the node type of `node` in `pType`.

node.doc: Node to query.

pType.doc: Pointer to return the node type.

cudaGraphNodeSetEnabled.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeSetEnabled(cudaGraphExec_t hGraphExec, cudaGraphNode_t hNode, unsigned int isEnabled)
cudaGraphNodeSetEnabled.doc:
Enables or disables the specified node in the given graphExec.

Sets `hNode` to be either enabled or disabled. Disabled nodes are functionally equivalent to empty nodes until they are reenabled. Existing node parameters are not affected by disabling/enabling the node.

The node is identified by the corresponding node `hNode` in the non-executable graph, from which the executable graph was instantiated.

`hNode` must not have been removed from the original graph.

The modifications only affect future launches of `hGraphExec`. Already enqueued or running launches of `hGraphExec` are not affected by this call. `hNode` is also not modified by this call.

hGraphExec.doc: The executable graph in which to set the specified node.

hNode.doc: Node from the graph from which graphExec was instantiated.

isEnabled.doc: Node is enabled if != 0, otherwise the node is disabled.

cudaGraphNodeSetParams.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphNodeSetParams(cudaGraphNode_t node, struct cudaGraphNodeParams * nodeParams)
cudaGraphNodeSetParams.doc:
Update a graph node’s parameters.

Sets the parameters of graph node `node` to `nodeParams`. The node type specified by `nodeParams->type` must match the type of `node`. `nodeParams` must be fully initialized and all unused bytes (reserved, padding) zeroed.

Modifying parameters is not supported for node types cudaGraphNodeTypeMemAlloc and cudaGraphNodeTypeMemFree.

node.doc: Node to set the parameters for.

cudaGraphReleaseUserObject.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphReleaseUserObject(cudaGraph_t graph, cudaUserObject_t object, unsigned int count = 1)
cudaGraphReleaseUserObject.doc:
Release a user object reference from a graph.

Releases user object references owned by a graph.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

graph.doc: The graph that will release the reference.

object.doc: The user object to release a reference for.

count.doc: The number of references to release, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

cudaGraphRemoveDependencies.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphRemoveDependencies(cudaGraph_t graph, const cudaGraphNode_t * from, const cudaGraphNode_t * to, const cudaGraphEdgeData * edgeData, size_t numDependencies)
cudaGraphRemoveDependencies.doc:
Removes dependency edges from a graph.

The number of `pDependencies` to be removed is defined by `numDependencies`. Elements in `pFrom` and `pTo` at corresponding indices define a dependency. Each node in `pFrom` and `pTo` must belong to `graph`.

If `numDependencies` is 0, elements in `pFrom` and `pTo` will be ignored. Specifying an edge that does not exist in the graph, with data matching `edgeData`, results in an error. `edgeData` is nullable, which is equivalent to passing default (zeroed) data for each edge.

graph.doc: Graph from which to remove dependencies.

from.doc: Array of nodes that provide the dependencies.

edgeData.doc: Optional array of edge data. If NULL, edge data is assumed to be default (zeroed).

numDependencies.doc: Number of dependencies to be removed.

cudaGraphRetainUserObject.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphRetainUserObject(cudaGraph_t graph, cudaUserObject_t object, unsigned int count = 1, unsigned int flags = 0)
cudaGraphRetainUserObject.doc:
Retain a reference to a user object from a graph.

Creates or moves user object references that will be owned by a CUDA graph.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

graph.doc: The graph to associate the reference with.

object.doc: The user object to retain a reference for.

count.doc: The number of references to add to the graph, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

flags.doc: The optional flag [cudaGraphUserObjectMove](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggae53f516fc65103fccb14c83184188157a96b13064f28cdb8932c782b94ab5802f) transfers references from the calling thread, rather than create new references. Pass 0 to create new references.

cudaGraphSetConditional.doc:
Sets the condition value associated with a conditional node.

Sets the condition value associated with a conditional node.

Note: `handle` must be associated with the same context as the kernel calling this function. Note: It is undefined behavior to have racing / possibly concurrent calls to [cudaGraphSetConditional](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__cudart__graph_1gade392fa316b963233219ab3caac9f1b3).

cudaGraphUpload.doc:
Uploads an executable graph in a stream.

Uploads `graphExec` to the device in `stream` without executing it. Uploads of the same `graphExec` will be serialized. Each upload is ordered behind both any previous work in `stream` and any previous launches of `graphExec`. Uses memory cached by `stream` to back the allocations owned by `graphExec`.

stream.doc: Stream in which to upload the graph.

cudaUserObjectCreate.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaUserObjectCreate(cudaUserObject_t * object_out, void * ptr, cudaHostFn_t destroy, unsigned int initialRefcount, unsigned int flags)
cudaUserObjectCreate.doc:
Create a user object.

Create a user object with the specified destructor callback and initial reference count. The initial references are owned by the caller.

Destructor callbacks cannot make CUDA API calls and should avoid blocking behavior, as they are executed by a shared internal thread. Another thread may be signaled to perform such actions, if it does not block forward progress of tasks scheduled through CUDA.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

object_out.doc: Location to return the user object handle.

ptr.doc: The pointer to pass to the destroy function.

destroy.doc: Callback to free the user object when it is no longer in use.

initialRefcount.doc: The initial refcount to create the object with, typically 1. The initial references are owned by the calling thread.

flags.doc: Currently it is required to pass [cudaUserObjectNoDestructorSync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggaf4748f36762263564ca8a7a47fd902bbaca181af9d994c9a5290b509175ea99fe), which is the only defined flag. This indicates that the destroy callback cannot be waited on by any CUDA API. Users requiring synchronization of the callback should signal its completion manually.

cudaUserObjectRelease.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaUserObjectRelease(cudaUserObject_t object, unsigned int count = 1)
cudaUserObjectRelease.doc:
Release a reference to a user object.

Releases user object references owned by the caller. The object’s destructor is invoked if the reference count reaches zero.

It is undefined behavior to release references not owned by the caller, or to use a user object handle after all references are released.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

count.doc: The number of references to release, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

cudaUserObjectRetain.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaUserObjectRetain(cudaUserObject_t object, unsigned int count = 1)
cudaUserObjectRetain.doc:
Retain a reference to a user object.

Retains new references to a user object. The new references are owned by the caller.

See CUDA User Objects in the CUDA C++ Programming Guide for more information on user objects.

count.doc: The number of references to retain, typically 1. Must be nonzero and not larger than INT_MAX.

cudaGraphicsMapResources.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphicsMapResources(int count, cudaGraphicsResource_t * resources, cudaStream_t stream = 0)
cudaGraphicsMapResources.doc:
Map graphics resources for access by CUDA.

Maps the `count` graphics resources in `resources` for access by CUDA.

The resources in `resources` may be accessed by CUDA until they are unmapped. The graphics API from which `resources` were registered should not access any resources while they are mapped by CUDA. If an application does so, the results are undefined.

This function provides the synchronization guarantee that any graphics calls issued before [cudaGraphicsMapResources()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__INTEROP.html#group__cudart__interop_1gaad8fbe74d02adefb8e7efb4971ee6322) will complete before any subsequent CUDA work issued in `stream` begins.

If `resources` contains any duplicate entries then [cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ac4673247aee4d1ab8d07871f376e0273) is returned. If any of `resources` are presently mapped for access by CUDA then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

cudaGraphicsResourceGetMappedMipmappedAr.doc:
Get a mipmapped array through which to access a mapped graphics resource.

Returns in `*mipmappedArray` a mipmapped array through which the mapped graphics resource `resource` may be accessed. The value set in `mipmappedArray` may change every time that `resource` is mapped.

If `resource` is not a texture then it cannot be accessed via an array and [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned. If `resource` is not mapped then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

mipmappedArray.doc: Returned mipmapped array through which `resource` may be accessed.

cudaGraphicsResourceGetMappedPointer.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphicsResourceGetMappedPointer(void * * devPtr, size_t * size, cudaGraphicsResource_t resource)
cudaGraphicsResourceGetMappedPointer.doc:
Get an device pointer through which to access a mapped graphics resource.

Returns in `*devPtr` a pointer through which the mapped graphics resource `resource` may be accessed. Returns in `*size` the size of the memory in bytes which may be accessed from that pointer. The value set in `devPtr` may change every time that `resource` is mapped.

If `resource` is not a buffer then it cannot be accessed via a pointer and [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned. If `resource` is not mapped then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

devPtr.doc: Returned pointer through which `resource` may be accessed.

size.doc: Returned size of the buffer accessible starting at `*devPtr`.

cudaGraphicsResourceSetMapFlags.doc:
Set usage flags for mapping a graphics resource.

Set `flags` for mapping the graphics resource `resource`.

Changes to `flags` will take effect the next time `resource` is mapped. The `flags` argument may be any of the following:

If `resource` is presently mapped for access by CUDA then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned. If `flags` is not one of the above values then [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) is returned.

resource.doc: Registered resource to set flags for.

cudaGraphicsSubResourceGetMappedArray.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphicsSubResourceGetMappedArray(cudaArray_t * array, cudaGraphicsResource_t resource, unsigned int arrayIndex, unsigned int mipLevel)
cudaGraphicsSubResourceGetMappedArray.doc:
Get an array through which to access a subresource of a mapped graphics resource.

Returns in `*array` an array through which the subresource of the mapped graphics resource `resource` which corresponds to array index `arrayIndex` and mipmap level `mipLevel` may be accessed. The value set in `array` may change every time that `resource` is mapped.

If `resource` is not a texture then it cannot be accessed via an array and [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned. If `arrayIndex` is not a valid array index for `resource` then [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) is returned. If `mipLevel` is not a valid mipmap level for `resource` then [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) is returned. If `resource` is not mapped then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

array.doc: Returned array through which a subresource of `resource` may be accessed.

arrayIndex.doc: Array index for array textures or cubemap face index as defined by [cudaGraphicsCubeFace](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gabf3ce16a621826a09263b8a58902fee8) for cubemap textures for the subresource to access.

mipLevel.doc: Mipmap level for the subresource to access.

cudaGraphicsUnmapResources.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGraphicsUnmapResources(int count, cudaGraphicsResource_t * resources, cudaStream_t stream = 0)
cudaGraphicsUnmapResources.doc:
Unmap graphics resources.

Unmaps the `count` graphics resources in `resources`.

Once unmapped, the resources in `resources` may not be accessed by CUDA until they are mapped again.

This function provides the synchronization guarantee that any CUDA work issued in `stream` before [cudaGraphicsUnmapResources()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__INTEROP.html#group__cudart__interop_1ga11988ab4431b11ddb7cbde7aedb60491) will complete before any subsequently issued graphics work begins.

If `resources` contains any duplicate entries then [cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ac4673247aee4d1ab8d07871f376e0273) is returned. If any of `resources` are not presently mapped for access by CUDA then [cudaErrorUnknown](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a2e491daacef266c7b3e3c1e140a6133c) is returned.

cudaGraphicsUnregisterResource.doc:
Unregisters a graphics resource for access by CUDA.

Unregisters the graphics resource `resource` so it is not accessible by CUDA unless registered again.

If `resource` is invalid then [cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ac4673247aee4d1ab8d07871f376e0273) is returned.

cudaGetFuncBySymbol.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGetFuncBySymbol(cudaFunction_t * functionPtr, const void * symbolPtr)
cudaGetFuncBySymbol.doc:
Get pointer to device entry function that matches entry function `symbolPtr`.

Returns in `functionPtr` the device entry function corresponding to the symbol `symbolPtr`.

symbolPtr.doc: Pointer to device entry function to search for.

cudaGetKernel.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGetKernel(cudaKernel_t * kernelPtr, const void * entryFuncAddr)
cudaGetKernel.doc:
Get pointer to device kernel that matches entry function `entryFuncAddr`.

Returns in `kernelPtr` the device kernel corresponding to the entry function `entryFuncAddr`.

Note that it is possible that there are multiple symbols belonging to different translation units with the same `entryFuncAddr` registered with this CUDA Runtime and so the order which the translation units are loaded and registered with the CUDA Runtime can lead to differing return pointers in `kernelPtr`. Suggested methods of ensuring uniqueness are to limit visibility of **global** device functions by using static or hidden visibility attribute in the respective translation units.

entryFuncAddr.doc: Address of device entry function to search kernel for.

cudaKernelSetAttributeForDevice.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaKernelSetAttributeForDevice(cudaKernel_t kernel, enum cudaFuncAttribute attr, int value, int device)
cudaKernelSetAttributeForDevice.doc:
Sets information about a kernel.

This call sets the value of a specified attribute `attr` on the kernel `kernel` for the requested device `device` to an integer value specified by `value`. This function returns [cudaSuccess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ae355f04607d824883b4a50662830d591) if the new value of the attribute could be successfully set. If the set fails, this call will return an error. Not all attributes can have values set. Attempting to set a value on a read-only attribute will result in an error ([cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c))

Note that attributes set using [cudaFuncSetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga317e77d2657abf915fd9ed03e75f3eb0) will override the attribute set by this API irrespective of whether the call to [cudaFuncSetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga317e77d2657abf915fd9ed03e75f3eb0) is made before or after this API call. Because of this and the stricter locking requirements mentioned below it is suggested that this call be used during the initialization path and not on each thread accessing `kernel` such as on kernel launches or on the critical path.

Valid values for `attr` are.

value.doc: Value to set.

device.doc: Device to set attribute of.

cudaLibraryEnumerateKernels.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryEnumerateKernels(cudaKernel_t * kernels, unsigned int numKernels, cudaLibrary_t lib)
cudaLibraryEnumerateKernels.doc:
Retrieve the kernel handles within a library.

Returns in `kernels` a maximum number of `numKernels` kernel handles within `lib`. The returned kernel handle becomes invalid when the library is unloaded.

kernels.doc: Buffer where the kernel handles are returned to.

numKernels.doc: Maximum number of kernel handles may be returned to the buffer.

cudaLibraryGetGlobal.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryGetGlobal(void * * dptr, size_t * bytes, cudaLibrary_t library, const char * name)
cudaLibraryGetGlobal.doc:
Returns a global device pointer.

Returns in `*dptr` and `*bytes` the base pointer and size of the global with name `name` for the requested library `library` and the current device. If no global for the requested name `name` exists, the call returns [cudaErrorSymbolNotFound](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a9d51ecb21a3081d01e078d136c137593). One of the parameters `dptr` or `bytes` (not both) can be NULL in which case it is ignored. The returned `dptr` cannot be passed to the Symbol APIs such as [cudaMemcpyToSymbol](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga9bcf02b53644eee2bef9983d807084c7), [cudaMemcpyFromSymbol](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga17ce3365ef7b6687a7d16c5b29de1f82), [cudaGetSymbolAddress](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga4f513be54d3794667c2017146b3d6a2b), or [cudaGetSymbolSize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga1d150bde14df4e291b520226fe475466).

dptr.doc: Returned global device pointer for the requested library.

cudaLibraryGetKernel.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryGetKernel(cudaKernel_t * pKernel, cudaLibrary_t library, const char * name)
cudaLibraryGetKernel.doc:
Returns a kernel handle.

Returns in `pKernel` the handle of the kernel with name `name` located in library `library`. If kernel handle is not found, the call returns [cudaErrorSymbolNotFound](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a9d51ecb21a3081d01e078d136c137593).

cudaLibraryGetKernelCount.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryGetKernelCount(unsigned int * count, cudaLibrary_t lib)
cudaLibraryGetKernelCount.doc:
Returns the number of kernels within a library.

Returns in `count` the number of kernels in `lib`.

count.doc: Number of kernels found within the library.

cudaLibraryGetManaged.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryGetManaged(void * * dptr, size_t * bytes, cudaLibrary_t library, const char * name)
cudaLibraryGetManaged.doc:
Returns a pointer to managed memory.

Returns in `*dptr` and `*bytes` the base pointer and size of the managed memory with name `name` for the requested library `library`. If no managed memory with the requested name `name` exists, the call returns [cudaErrorSymbolNotFound](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a9d51ecb21a3081d01e078d136c137593). One of the parameters `dptr` or `bytes` (not both) can be NULL in which case it is ignored. Note that managed memory for library `library` is shared across devices and is registered when the library is loaded. The returned `dptr` cannot be passed to the Symbol APIs such as [cudaMemcpyToSymbol](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga9bcf02b53644eee2bef9983d807084c7), [cudaMemcpyFromSymbol](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga17ce3365ef7b6687a7d16c5b29de1f82), [cudaGetSymbolAddress](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga4f513be54d3794667c2017146b3d6a2b), or [cudaGetSymbolSize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga1d150bde14df4e291b520226fe475466).

dptr.doc: Returned pointer to the managed memory.

library.doc: Library to retrieve managed memory from.

name.doc: Name of managed memory to retrieve.

cudaLibraryGetUnifiedFunction.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryGetUnifiedFunction(void * * fptr, cudaLibrary_t library, const char * symbol)
cudaLibraryGetUnifiedFunction.doc:
Returns a pointer to a unified function.

Returns in `*fptr` the function pointer to a unified function denoted by `symbol`. If no unified function with name `symbol` exists, the call returns [cudaErrorSymbolNotFound](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a9d51ecb21a3081d01e078d136c137593). If there is no device with attribute [cudaDeviceProp::unifiedFunctionPointers](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaDeviceProp.html#structcudadeviceprop_1a9f94309e6d30a640821cc9de9591e565) present in the system, the call may return [cudaErrorSymbolNotFound](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a9d51ecb21a3081d01e078d136c137593).

fptr.doc: Returned pointer to a unified function.

library.doc: Library to retrieve function pointer memory from.

symbol.doc: Name of function pointer to retrieve.

cudaLibraryLoadData.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryLoadData(cudaLibrary_t * library, const void * code, enum cudaJitOption * jitOptions, void * * jitOptionsValues, unsigned int numJitOptions, enum cudaLibraryOption * libraryOptions, void * * libraryOptionValues, unsigned int numLibraryOptions)
cudaLibraryLoadData.doc:
Load a library with specified code and options.

Takes a pointer `code` and loads the corresponding library `library` based on the application defined library loading mode:

These environment variables are described in the CUDA programming guide under the “CUDA environment variables” section.

The `code` may be a *cubin* or *fatbin* as output by **nvcc**, or a NULL-terminated *PTX*, either as output by **nvcc** or hand-written, or *Tile* IR data. A fatbin should also contain relocatable code when doing separate compilation. Please also see the documentation for nvrtc (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvrtc/index.html>), nvjitlink (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvjitlink/index.html>), and nvfatbin (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvfatbin/index.html>) for more information on generating loadable code at runtime.

Options are passed as an array via `jitOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `jitOptionsValues`. The number of total JIT options is supplied via `numJitOptions`. Any outputs will be returned via `jitOptionsValues`.

Library load options are passed as an array via `libraryOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `libraryOptionValues`. The number of total library load options is supplied via `numLibraryOptions`.

cudaLibraryLoadFromFile.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaLibraryLoadFromFile(cudaLibrary_t * library, const char * fileName, enum cudaJitOption * jitOptions, void * * jitOptionsValues, unsigned int numJitOptions, enum cudaLibraryOption * libraryOptions, void * * libraryOptionValues, unsigned int numLibraryOptions)
cudaLibraryLoadFromFile.doc:
Load a library with specified file and options.

Takes a pointer `code` and loads the corresponding library `library` based on the application defined library loading mode:

These environment variables are described in the CUDA programming guide under the “CUDA environment variables” section.

The file should be a *cubin* file as output by **nvcc**, or a *PTX* file either as output by **nvcc** or handwritten, or a *fatbin* file as output by **nvcc** or hand-written, or *Tile* IR file. A fatbin should also contain relocatable code when doing separate compilation. Please also see the documentation for nvrtc (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvrtc/index.html>), nvjitlink (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvjitlink/index.html>), and nvfatbin (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvfatbin/index.html>) for more information on generating loadable code at runtime.

Options are passed as an array via `jitOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `jitOptionsValues`. The number of total options is supplied via `numJitOptions`. Any outputs will be returned via `jitOptionsValues`.

Library load options are passed as an array via `libraryOptions` and any corresponding parameters are passed in `libraryOptionValues`. The number of total library load options is supplied via `numLibraryOptions`.

cudaLibraryUnload.doc:
Unloads a library.

Unloads the library specified with `library`.

cudaFabricOpErrorStatusCount.signature: __device__ cudaError_t cudaFabricOpErrorStatusCount(void * status, cudaFabricOpStatusSource statusSource, unsigned int * count)
cudaFabricOpErrorStatusCount.doc:
Get the number of errors for a fabric operation.

Given the pointer to the `status` field obtained from fabric operation completion object, return the total count of errors.

status.doc: The pointer to the status field obtained from fabric operation completion object.

statusSource.doc: The type of the fabric operation completion object.

count.doc: The number of errors in the decoded status field.

cudaFabricOpErrorStatusGet.signature: __device__ cudaError_t cudaFabricOpErrorStatusGet(void * status, cudaFabricOpStatusSource statusSource, unsigned int statusIndex, cudaFabricOpStatusInfo * statusInfo)
cudaFabricOpErrorStatusGet.doc:
Get the error status of a fabric operation.

Given a pointer to the `status` field obtained from a fabric operation completion object, retrieves the error at index `statusIndex` in the decoded `status` field and writes it to `statusInfo`.

`statusIndex` must be in the range [0, statusCount), where statusCount is the value returned via the `count` parameter of [cudaFabricOpErrorStatusCount](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__FABRIC.html#group__cudart__fabric_1gabd406f0b76f38607e3cfb4e9925c395b).

status.doc: Pointer to the status field from the fabric operation completion object.

statusSource.doc: The type of the fabric operation completion object.

statusIndex.doc: Index of the error to retrieve (0-based; selects which of the decoded errors to return).

statusInfo.doc: Pointer to `cudaFabricOpStatusInfo` where the decoded error information is returned.

cudaArrayGetInfo.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaArrayGetInfo(struct cudaChannelFormatDesc * desc, struct cudaExtent * extent, unsigned int * flags, cudaArray_t array)
cudaArrayGetInfo.doc:
Gets info about the specified cudaArray.

Returns in `*desc`, `*extent` and `*flags` respectively, the type, shape and flags of `array`.

Any of `*desc`, `*extent` and `*flags` may be specified as NULL.

extent.doc: Returned array shape. 2D arrays will have depth of zero.

cudaArrayGetMemoryRequirements.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaArrayGetMemoryRequirements(struct cudaArrayMemoryRequirements * memoryRequirements, cudaArray_t array, int device)
cudaArrayGetMemoryRequirements.doc:
Returns the memory requirements of a CUDA array.

Returns the memory requirements of a CUDA array in `memoryRequirements` If the CUDA array is not allocated with flag [cudaArrayDeferredMapping](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga91a50795515848406a89c2e6cef2fb02) [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) will be returned.

The returned value in [cudaArrayMemoryRequirements::size](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaArrayMemoryRequirements.html#structcudaarraymemoryrequirements_1acff0bc12daa05c6c40892a2187befd87) represents the total size of the CUDA array. The returned value in [cudaArrayMemoryRequirements::alignment](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaArrayMemoryRequirements.html#structcudaarraymemoryrequirements_1a37898b13b500d39e4a43d0ee04cf0ef3) represents the alignment necessary for mapping the CUDA array.

array.doc: CUDA array to get the memory requirements of.

device.doc: Device to get the memory requirements for.

cudaArrayGetPlane.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaArrayGetPlane(cudaArray_t * pPlaneArray, cudaArray_t hArray, unsigned int planeIdx)
cudaArrayGetPlane.doc:
Gets a CUDA array plane from a CUDA array.

Returns in `pPlaneArray` a CUDA array that represents a single format plane of the CUDA array `hArray`.

If `planeIdx` is greater than the maximum number of planes in this array or if the array does not have a multi-planar format e.g: [cudaChannelFormatKindNV12](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga8085eac5cb54b4228f3619a60f235119ac89d051aff61fb1bd60a69fdd82a97c2), then [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) is returned.

Note that if the `hArray` has format [cudaChannelFormatKindNV12](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga8085eac5cb54b4228f3619a60f235119ac89d051aff61fb1bd60a69fdd82a97c2), then passing in 0 for `planeIdx` returns a CUDA array of the same size as `hArray` but with one 8-bit channel and [cudaChannelFormatKindUnsigned](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga8085eac5cb54b4228f3619a60f235119a240d73fa2dc05cbaa58f093f169ab3d4) as its format kind. If 1 is passed for `planeIdx`, then the returned CUDA array has half the height and width of `hArray` with two 8-bit channels and [cudaChannelFormatKindUnsigned](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga8085eac5cb54b4228f3619a60f235119a240d73fa2dc05cbaa58f093f169ab3d4) as its format kind.

pPlaneArray.doc: Returned CUDA array referenced by the `planeIdx`.

cudaArrayGetSparseProperties.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaArrayGetSparseProperties(struct cudaArraySparseProperties * sparseProperties, cudaArray_t array)
cudaArrayGetSparseProperties.doc:
Returns the layout properties of a sparse CUDA array.

Returns the layout properties of a sparse CUDA array in `sparseProperties`. If the CUDA array is not allocated with flag [cudaArraySparse](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga42c353686a15da063dc7722594ae4bff) [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) will be returned.

If the returned value in [cudaArraySparseProperties::flags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaArraySparseProperties.html#structcudaarraysparseproperties_1a44c8728469d60e511aceb4ba7086c164) contains [cudaArraySparsePropertiesSingleMipTail](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga6820071ffa1300699897eab8d319e4d9), then [cudaArraySparseProperties::miptailSize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaArraySparseProperties.html#structcudaarraysparseproperties_1a22cfa4ad83195f0e9585303c988bb886) represents the total size of the array. Otherwise, it will be zero. Also, the returned value in [cudaArraySparseProperties::miptailFirstLevel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaArraySparseProperties.html#structcudaarraysparseproperties_1ab6909e5db55b866477b6cc16fb02f9d3) is always zero. Note that the `array` must have been allocated using [cudaMallocArray](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga6728eb7dc25f332f50bdb16a19620d3d) or [cudaMalloc3DArray](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga948143cf2423a072ac6a31fb635efd88). For CUDA arrays obtained using ::cudaMipmappedArrayGetLevel, [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) will be returned. Instead, [cudaMipmappedArrayGetSparseProperties](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga96d65849f80adb87d239f68756ed5b14) must be used to obtain the sparse properties of the entire CUDA mipmapped array to which `array` belongs to.

array.doc: The CUDA array to get the sparse properties of.

cudaFree.doc:
Frees memory on the device.

Frees the memory space pointed to by `devPtr`, which must have been returned by a previous call to one of the following memory allocation APIs - [cudaMalloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae63c9974e34b14fd750efd91b32f405b), [cudaMallocPitch()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga32bd7a39135594788a542ae72217775c), [cudaMallocManaged()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gaec54cd99121bfb36af81257463b5cb81), [cudaMallocAsync()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1gabbf70065888d61853c047513baa14081), [cudaMallocFromPoolAsync()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1ga871003f518e27ec92f7b331307fa32d4).

Note - This API will not perform any implicit synchronization when the pointer was allocated with [cudaMallocAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1gabbf70065888d61853c047513baa14081) or [cudaMallocFromPoolAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1ga871003f518e27ec92f7b331307fa32d4). Callers must ensure that all accesses to these pointer have completed before invoking [cudaFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6). For best performance and memory reuse, users should use [cudaFreeAsync](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY__POOLS.html#group__cudart__memory__pools_1ga3398a689c75448c1bf99368e490ac878) to free memory allocated via the stream ordered memory allocator. For all other pointers, this API may perform implicit synchronization.

If [cudaFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6)(`devPtr`) has already been called before, an error is returned. If `devPtr` is 0, no operation is performed. [cudaFree()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6) returns ::cudaErrorValue in case of failure.

The device version of [cudaFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6) cannot be used with a `*devPtr` allocated using the host API, and vice versa.

cudaFreeArray.doc:
Frees an array on the device.

Frees the CUDA array `array`, which must have been returned by a previous call to [cudaMallocArray()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga6728eb7dc25f332f50bdb16a19620d3d). If `devPtr` is 0, no operation is performed.

cudaFreeHost.doc:
Frees page-locked memory.

Frees the memory space pointed to by `hostPtr`, which must have been returned by a previous call to [cudaMallocHost()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gaab84100ae1fa1b12eaca660207ef585b) or [cudaHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gab65da58f444e7230d3322b6126bb4902).

cudaFreeMipmappedArray.doc:
Frees a mipmapped array on the device.

Frees the CUDA mipmapped array `mipmappedArray`, which must have been returned by a previous call to [cudaMallocMipmappedArray()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga9abd550dd3f655473d2640dc85be9774). If `devPtr` is 0, no operation is performed.

cudaGetMipmappedArrayLevel.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGetMipmappedArrayLevel(cudaArray_t * levelArray, cudaMipmappedArray_const_t mipmappedArray, unsigned int level)
cudaGetMipmappedArrayLevel.doc:
Gets a mipmap level of a CUDA mipmapped array.

Returns in `*levelArray` a CUDA array that represents a single mipmap level of the CUDA mipmapped array `mipmappedArray`.

If `level` is greater than the maximum number of levels in this mipmapped array, [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c) is returned.

If `mipmappedArray` is NULL, [cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ac4673247aee4d1ab8d07871f376e0273) is returned.

cudaGetSymbolAddress.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGetSymbolAddress(void * * devPtr, const void * symbol)
cudaGetSymbolAddress.doc:
Finds the address associated with a CUDA symbol.

Returns in `*devPtr` the address of symbol `symbol` on the device. `symbol` is a variable that resides in global or constant memory space. If `symbol` cannot be found, or if `symbol` is not declared in the global or constant memory space, `*devPtr` is unchanged and the error [cudaErrorInvalidSymbol](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a01a4a97f3060ec714ffa9dd650b9213a) is returned.

devPtr.doc: Return device pointer associated with symbol.

cudaGetSymbolSize.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaGetSymbolSize(size_t * size, const void * symbol)
cudaGetSymbolSize.doc:
Finds the size of the object associated with a CUDA symbol.

Returns in `*size` the size of symbol `symbol`. `symbol` is a variable that resides in global or constant memory space. If `symbol` cannot be found, or if `symbol` is not declared in global or constant memory space, `*size` is unchanged and the error [cudaErrorInvalidSymbol](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a01a4a97f3060ec714ffa9dd650b9213a) is returned.

size.doc: Size of object associated with symbol.

cudaHostAlloc.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaHostAlloc(void * * pHost, size_t size, unsigned int flags)
cudaHostAlloc.doc:
Allocates page-locked memory on the host.

Allocates `size` bytes of host memory that is page-locked and accessible to the device. The driver tracks the virtual memory ranges allocated with this function and automatically accelerates calls to functions such as [cudaMemcpy()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac263dbe6574220cc776b45438fc351e8). Since the memory can be accessed directly by the device, it can be read or written with much higher bandwidth than pageable memory obtained with functions such as ::malloc(). Allocating excessive amounts of pinned memory may degrade system performance, since it reduces the amount of memory available to the system for paging. As a result, this function is best used sparingly to allocate staging areas for data exchange between host and device.

The `flags` parameter enables different options to be specified that affect the allocation, as follows.

All of these flags are orthogonal to one another: a developer may allocate memory that is portable, mapped and/or write-combined with no restrictions.

In order for the [cudaHostAllocMapped](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga01e600c738b962c8f973dda7708f7a70) flag to have any effect, the CUDA context must support the [cudaDeviceMapHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga3762be9cccdd809a4ca128354fd134b0) flag, which can be checked via [cudaGetDeviceFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1gaf830794caf068b71638c6182bba8f77a). The [cudaDeviceMapHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga3762be9cccdd809a4ca128354fd134b0) flag is implicitly set for contexts created via the runtime API.

The [cudaHostAllocMapped](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga01e600c738b962c8f973dda7708f7a70) flag may be specified on CUDA contexts for devices that do not support mapped pinned memory. The failure is deferred to [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) because the memory may be mapped into other CUDA contexts via the [cudaHostAllocPortable](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gac46ce76be41cf79774331cc8cfceb52b) flag.

Memory allocated by this function must be freed with [cudaFreeHost()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga71c078689c17627566b2a91989184969).

cudaHostGetDevicePointer.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaHostGetDevicePointer(void * * pDevice, void * pHost, unsigned int flags)
cudaHostGetDevicePointer.doc:
Passes back device pointer of mapped host memory allocated by cudaHostAlloc or registered by cudaHostRegister.

Passes back the device pointer corresponding to the mapped, pinned host buffer allocated by [cudaHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gab65da58f444e7230d3322b6126bb4902) or registered by [cudaHostRegister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae8d5c17670f16ac4fc8fcb4181cb490c).

[cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) will fail if the [cudaDeviceMapHost](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga3762be9cccdd809a4ca128354fd134b0) flag was not specified before deferred context creation occurred, or if called on a device that does not support mapped, pinned memory.

For devices that have a non-zero value for the device attribute [cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cdab08e379a7a038dc8134914702c223f69), the memory can also be accessed from the device using the host pointer `pHost`. The device pointer returned by [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) may or may not match the original host pointer `pHost` and depends on the devices visible to the application. If all devices visible to the application have a non-zero value for the device attribute, the device pointer returned by [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) will match the original pointer `pHost`. If any device visible to the application has a zero value for the device attribute, the device pointer returned by [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) will not match the original host pointer `pHost`, but it will be suitable for use on all devices provided Unified Virtual Addressing is enabled. In such systems, it is valid to access the memory using either pointer on devices that have a non-zero value for the device attribute. Note however that such devices should access the memory using only of the two pointers and not both.

`flags` provides for future releases. For now, it must be set to 0.

pDevice.doc: Returned device pointer for mapped memory.

flags.doc: Flags for extensions (must be 0 for now).

cudaHostGetFlags.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaHostGetFlags(unsigned int * pFlags, void * pHost)
cudaHostGetFlags.doc:
Passes back flags used to allocate pinned host memory allocated by cudaHostAlloc.

[cudaHostGetFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac470e9220559109f5088d9a01c0aeeda) will fail if the input pointer does not reside in an address range allocated by [cudaHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gab65da58f444e7230d3322b6126bb4902).

cudaHostRegister.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaHostRegister(void * ptr, size_t size, unsigned int flags)
cudaHostRegister.doc:
Registers an existing host memory range for use by CUDA.

Page-locks the memory range specified by `ptr` and `size` and maps it for the device(s) as specified by `flags`. This memory range also is added to the same tracking mechanism as [cudaHostAlloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gab65da58f444e7230d3322b6126bb4902) to automatically accelerate calls to functions such as [cudaMemcpy()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac263dbe6574220cc776b45438fc351e8). Since the memory can be accessed directly by the device, it can be read or written with much higher bandwidth than pageable memory that has not been registered. Page-locking excessive amounts of memory may degrade system performance, since it reduces the amount of memory available to the system for paging. As a result, this function is best used sparingly to register staging areas for data exchange between host and device.

On systems where ::pageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables is true, [cudaHostRegister](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae8d5c17670f16ac4fc8fcb4181cb490c) will not page-lock the memory range specified by `ptr` but only populate unpopulated pages.

[cudaHostRegister](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae8d5c17670f16ac4fc8fcb4181cb490c) is supported only on I/O coherent devices that have a non-zero value for the device attribute [cudaDevAttrHostRegisterSupported](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda6ea4a004a336c3c95b6ff06ec6269e29).

The `flags` parameter enables different options to be specified that affect the allocation, as follows.

All of these flags are orthogonal to one another: a developer may page-lock memory that is portable or mapped with no restrictions.

The CUDA context must have been created with the ::cudaMapHost flag in order for the [cudaHostRegisterMapped](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga838b73458521c60f502efd19db0e365d) flag to have any effect.

The [cudaHostRegisterMapped](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga838b73458521c60f502efd19db0e365d) flag may be specified on CUDA contexts for devices that do not support mapped pinned memory. The failure is deferred to [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) because the memory may be mapped into other CUDA contexts via the [cudaHostRegisterPortable](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga36977255e5c778f7e4362d32d6b1cecd) flag.

For devices that have a non-zero value for the device attribute [cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cdab08e379a7a038dc8134914702c223f69), the memory can also be accessed from the device using the host pointer `ptr`. The device pointer returned by [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) may or may not match the original host pointer `ptr` and depends on the devices visible to the application. If all devices visible to the application have a non-zero value for the device attribute, the device pointer returned by [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) will match the original pointer `ptr`. If any device visible to the application has a zero value for the device attribute, the device pointer returned by [cudaHostGetDevicePointer()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gac00502b44e5f1bdc0b424487ebb08db0) will not match the original host pointer `ptr`, but it will be suitable for use on all devices provided Unified Virtual Addressing is enabled. In such systems, it is valid to access the memory using either pointer on devices that have a non-zero value for the device attribute. Note however that such devices should access the memory using only of the two pointers and not both.

The memory page-locked by this function must be unregistered with [cudaHostUnregister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga81fd4101862bbefdb42a62d60e515eea).

ptr.doc: Host pointer to memory to page-lock.

size.doc: Size in bytes of the address range to page-lock in bytes.

cudaHostUnregister.doc:
Unregisters a memory range that was registered with cudaHostRegister.

Unmaps the memory range whose base address is specified by `ptr`, and makes it pageable again.

The base address must be the same one specified to [cudaHostRegister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae8d5c17670f16ac4fc8fcb4181cb490c).

cudaMalloc.doc:
Allocate memory on the device.

Allocates `size` bytes of linear memory on the device and returns in `*devPtr` a pointer to the allocated memory. The allocated memory is suitably aligned for any kind of variable. The memory is not cleared. [cudaMalloc()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae63c9974e34b14fd750efd91b32f405b) returns [cudaErrorMemoryAllocation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038af210f50ae7f17f655e0504929606add9) in case of failure.

The device version of [cudaFree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga8ac8e719117293943b2707160156d8c6) cannot be used with a `*devPtr` allocated using the host API, and vice versa.

devPtr.doc: Pointer to allocated device memory.

cudaMalloc3D.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaMalloc3D(struct cudaPitchedPtr * pitchedDevPtr, struct cudaExtent extent)
cudaMalloc3D.doc:
Allocates logical 1D, 2D, or 3D memory objects on the device.

Allocates at least `width` \* `height` \* `depth` bytes of linear memory on the device and returns a [cudaPitchedPtr](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaPitchedPtr.html#structcudapitchedptr) in which `ptr` is a pointer to the allocated memory. The function may pad the allocation to ensure hardware alignment requirements are met. The pitch returned in the `pitch` field of `pitchedDevPtr` is the width in bytes of the allocation.

The returned [cudaPitchedPtr](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaPitchedPtr.html#structcudapitchedptr) contains additional fields `xsize` and `ysize`, the logical width and height of the allocation, which are equivalent to the `width` and `height` `extent` parameters provided by the programmer during allocation.

For allocations of 2D and 3D objects, it is highly recommended that programmers perform allocations using [cudaMalloc3D()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga188300e599ded65c925e79eab2a57347) or [cudaMallocPitch()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga32bd7a39135594788a542ae72217775c). Due to alignment restrictions in the hardware, this is especially true if the application will be performing memory copies involving 2D or 3D objects (whether linear memory or CUDA arrays).

pitchedDevPtr.doc: Pointer to allocated pitched device memory.

extent.doc: Requested allocation size (`width` field in bytes).

cudaMalloc3DArray.signature: __host__ cudaError_t cudaMalloc3DArray(cudaArray_t * array, const struct cudaChannelFormatDesc * desc, struct cudaExtent extent, unsigned int flags = 0)
cudaMalloc3DArray.doc:
Allocate an array on the device.

Allocates a CUDA array according to the [cudaChannelFormatDesc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaChannelFormatDesc.html#structcudachannelformatdesc) structure `desc` and returns a handle to the new CUDA array in `*array`.

The [cudaChannelFormatDesc](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaChannelFormatDesc.html#structcudachannelformatdesc) is defined as:

[cudaMalloc3DArray()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga948143cf2423a072ac6a31fb635efd88) can allocate the following:

The `flags` parameter enables different options to be specified that affect the allocation, as follows.

The width, height and depth extents must meet certain size requirements as listed in the following table. All values are specified in elements.

Note that 2D CUDA arrays have different size requirements if the [cudaArrayTextureGather](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga142b19a14d56a03b1e410430aa5202d1) flag is set. In that case, the valid range for (width, height, depth) is ((1,maxTexture2DGather[0]), (1,maxTexture2DGather[1]), 0).
